latest.title: ApocaHUD43 1.0.2
latest.notes:
Keeps Apocalypter's HUD on the screen edges at any aspect ratio (4:3, 16:10, 21:9).

The game lays its HUD out for 16:9 with everything anchored to the screen centre, so on 4:3 the bottom row (weapon card, survival card, quick items, ammo / nuts / armour, compass) hangs above the bottom of the screen. mods.name: Apocasaver
mods.author: DeonUrist
mods.summary: Autosave into the slot you are playing and give your saves names.

latest.title: Apocasaver 2.0.2
latest.notes:
Apocasaver 2.0.2 restores the intended save policy: saving is not rejected because an optional feature or a completeness
check is uncertain. Missing native confirmations, unexpected FSM states, companion compatibility problems and cleanup
uncertainty are log warnings. Prior useful records are retained; uncertain cleanup is skipped.

When rebuilding cannot initialize, the game saves normally without deleting the destination. If a completion confirmation
is missing, available save data is written instead of being rejected after 60 seconds. Actual disk persistence failures
still restore the previous save from backup and show a failure warning.

CleanSaves remains off by default and includes abandoned Apocapatrol vehicles/items when supported. A candidate that becomes
protected during saving is kept in both the game world and the saved registration arrays.

Includes the 2.0.1 destroyed-plugin-component startup fix. Update Apocasaver and restart the game; no companion update is
required for the installed versions tested. Full interactive/long-session validation remains pending.

mods.name: Engine Sim
mods.author: Wad67
mods.summary: Replaces the recorded engine sounds with a live engine simulation (engine-sim) built from the fitted engine: cylinders, exhaust, wear, misfires, rev limiter.

latest.title: Engine Sim 1.3.0
latest.notes:
# Engine Sim 1.3.0

## Engines with the key off

- **Every fitted engine is simulated, running or not** (up to `MaxEngines`, engines that are turning or have
  the key on first, then the nearest). An engine turned with the key off, rolling in gear or being pushed, is
  heard turning over, without ignition.
- The game's sound bridge (`NWH2_RES2`) switches the engine sound object off whenever the ignition is off,
  which silenced an engine still turning. For a simulated engine it now sees the ignition on for the length of
  its own update, so the sound stays, and the sound component's own engine loops stay muted.

## Simulated drivetrain

### The engine against its load

The game's engine step pulls the engine towards the drivetrain's speed with a correcting torque and hands
that whole torque to the clutch, but then moves the engine by only its share of the whole drivetrain's
inertia. With any real load behind the clutch the engine barely changed speed. On the road the tyres'
reaction covered this up; with nothing reacting (a wheel off the ground, a flywheel) the drivetrain was fed
the correction step after step until it caught up, and the engine never felt it.

- **In gear, the engine now turns on its own inertia**, driven by its torque and loaded by exactly the torque
  it passes through the clutch.
  - **Clutch held:** its momentum goes into the drivetrain and the two settle at one speed. A heavy enough
    load stalls it: first gear against a stopped load, or reverse at speed.
  - **Clutch slipping:** the engine is dragged by the friction torque alone, and its revs fall into the next
    gear on a shift.
  - **Neutral:** nothing behind the clutch takes the torque, so the game's own step is kept.
- **The starter** can't turn an engine held against a heavy load in gear, and clicks.

### Clutch

- The clutch holds at least 2.5 times the engine's peak torque (the game scales it down with condition, to a
  few N m on a worn engine). It used to be overwritten with that every frame; a vehicle that sets a stronger
  clutch of its own now keeps it.

### Wheels

- **Wheel inertia.** The game's drivetrain takes each wheel's inertia once as the vehicle starts up, before
  the wheel has worked it out from its mass and radius. A wheel set up at runtime (a vehicle built by another
  mod) was driven as if weightless. Such wheels now get half m r squared.
- **Solid axles.** A wheel without suspension travel can't take up a change of size. When a bigger wheel went
  on (fitted, or set again as a save loads) its collision mesh grew into the ground, burying it or throwing the
  vehicle. The vehicle is now lifted by as much as the wheel would sink, as it would be jacked up to fit it.

## Parts for building vehicles

New components a vehicle can carry, added by a vehicle mod (for example from a SigmaMod `.json`). They work
with or without the simulated drivetrain. See the README for their fields.

- **`WheelCoupling`**: two wheels turned together outside the game's drivetrain, which only knows a tree from
  the gearbox down to the wheels. A belt from a flywheel to another axle, a shaft, or a solid axle.
  - A ratio (b turns `ratio` times as fast as a), a capacity in N m, and an engagement from 0 to 1, for a belt
    tensioner or clutch lever.
  - It works through the wheels' torque, as the game's drivetrain does. A wheel on the ground drives the car,
    the road loads the coupling, and the engine feels it through the belt. Couplings sharing a wheel add up.
  - With `VerboseLog`, a `[coupling]` line every 5 s: the torque passed, both sides' speeds through the ratio,
    and the driven wheel's ground contact, load, grip and road force.
- **`Belt`**: draws a belt round two pulleys, straight along the outer tangents and wrapped round each.
  - The tensioner (the coupling's engagement) takes up the slack. Released, the lower run hangs and the belt
    stands still; tightened, it straightens and the driving rim drags it round.
  - Without a material i
